my_lead: 9b (3-(6-chloro-9H-purin-9-yl)dodecan-1-ol): abstract names it the most potent and a promising lead; used in the xenograft

reactions.issue: Section 6.1.26: 6-chloro-9H-purine (0.2 mmol) + (E)-dodec-2-enal (0.3 mmol), L-proline/benzoic acid, MeOH, rt 24 h, then NaBH4 at 0 C, 77.5% (52.4 mg). One-pot aza-Michael/reduction is a single procedure; L-proline, benzoic acid, NaBH4, MeOH correctly omitted. Product is racemic (the rac-/R-/S- series in Table 2; the (R)-9b is a separate asymmetric route with Cat. II).

leaf_issues: 6-chloropurine and (E)-dodec-2-enal: supported only by the general sentence 'All commercial reagents and solvents were purchased from commercial suppliers and used without further purification' (6.1 General Methods). Nothing is prepared or cited elsewhere.
notes: SMILES checked: OCCC(CCCCCCCCC)n1cnc2c(Cl)ncnc21 = 12-carbon chain with OH on C1 and purin-9-yl on C3 (3 + 9 carbons), N9-linked 6-chloropurine; 6-chloropurine SMILES Clc1ncnc2[nH]cnc12 correct. Note the abstract's 'all (R)-configured ... more potent' means (R)-9b exists as an alternative (asymmetric, Scheme 2, also one pot) but the lead rule gives 9b as named (racemate), which the paper itself tested as 'rac-9b'. Heading 6.1.27 for (R)-9b has a typo ('decan-1-ol') in the paper; irrelevant here.
